attributes.readMe:
## Shipment Status (SS)

Six states: label created, in transit, out for delivery, delivered, exception, returned to sender.

**Why this is not the order's status.** One order can carry two shipments at different stages — item A from the London arch, item B from the Manchester 3PL. Collapsing the two enums into one makes that unrepresentable, so they stay separate and the order's status is a summary of its packages rather than a copy of one.

`SHIPMENT_PIPELINE` excludes `exception` and `returned_to_sender` on purpose. A package sitting in exception has not progressed, and a rail that kept advancing while nothing happened would be a lying affordance. `isShipmentException()` is exported so consumers can ask directly.

### Example

`SHP-2026-0146` is out for delivery; `SHP-2026-0142` is the exception case (a failed delivery attempt) and shows the stalled rail.

### Non-goals

Carrier status codes are not normalised here. A carrier scan carries its own code and description on `TrackingEventField`; mapping every carrier vocabulary onto this enum is integration work and belongs with whatever fetches the scans.
